clue.text: Astute in flushing it out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of flushing it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd at rooting out a hidden secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the end of a phrasal verb 'flushing it out', but it is the anagram signal for FLUSHING IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An astute person shows perception and penetration, which is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Regarding charge? One's postponed endlessly

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's (one has) links it to what follows

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the phrase for postponed is dropped

parts.note: something postponed is put on ice

explanation.surface: A query about an accusation, followed by news that someone's case is delayed indefinitely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the last letter from ON ICE, leaving ONIC after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic means relating to ions, atoms carrying an electrical charge; the question mark flags the pun on a legal charge.

clue.text: It's racy, perverted and lecherous

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of something risqué, kinky and lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' reads as part of the description but signals an anagram of IT'S RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs were lustful woodland gods, so behaviour like theirs is lewd and lustful.

clue.text: Gang sometime ploughed up field of earth

indicators.note: soil that is ploughed up is turned over and churned, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A farm gang once turned over a field of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface field is farmland; the definition means a field of study or a force field concerning the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Geomagnetism is the planet's magnetic field and its scientific study, so a field relating to the globe.

clue.text: Ugly creature little expected to receive love

indicators.note: the small word is expected to take something into itself, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A homely creature with low expectations hopes to be loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Warty amphibians are traditionally thought of as unlovely beasts, an example of an ugly creature.

clue.text: Unlikely to rise, being avoided, having ignored request for silence about holidays

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters go around the time-off word
having ignored means the letters for the call for quiet are left out

parts.note: someone being avoided is shunned
sh is the hushing sound asking for quiet
leave is time off work, holidays

explanation.surface: A person avoided and shushed is sent away on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ignored' leaves UNNED, which 'about' wraps round the holiday word; the definition describes bread made without yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleavened bread is made without yeast, so the dough does not swell up in the oven.

clue.text: A verb in German certainly indicates a modern language

parts.note: ja is German for yes, certainly
V is the grammar abbreviation for verb

explanation.surface: A grammar point: a German verb signals a contemporary tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The language is not a spoken one but a computer programming language.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is a widely used programming language, a modern coding tongue rather than a spoken one.

clue.text: Aim to interrupt a lot of discussion in items for meetings

indicators.note: to interrupt means the purpose word breaks into the talk letters

parts.note: gas is informal for lots of idle chat
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: Someone with a purpose butts into a long debate over meeting business.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lists of business to be dealt with at a committee session, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Flower a stupid sheep turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the words for daft and the male animal are read backwards

parts.note: silly means stupid
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A dim-witted sheep has toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses the daft-ram phrase to MARYLLIS; 'Flower' is a bloom, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulb plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: New court case not about to get support all over the country

indicators.note: not means the letter for about is left out of the lawsuit word

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit, a court case
C stands for circa, about
to ally is to back or support

explanation.surface: A fresh lawsuit is about to win backing everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about' removes C (circa) from ACTION, giving ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done nationally happens throughout the whole nation, everywhere in the land.

clue.text: Take a chance with article under test

parts.note: to bet is to gamble, take a chance
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gamble on an item that is being trialled.
explanation.definitionFit: Software in beta is released for trialling before its final version, so it is still being tried out.

clue.text: Dicky is eloquent about a book of dubious merit

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap around the following pair
dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so these letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Dicky speaks fluently about a poorly regarded book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is British slang for unsound, the anagram signal; 'about' puts AB inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to doubt or suspicion is of uncertain worth or honesty.

clue.text: See 15
No source for dairy product in peanut-based dish in this period of time

indicators.note: in means the trimmed dairy word sits inside the dish

parts.note: satay is skewered meat with peanut sauce

indicators.note: no source means the opening letter is dropped from the word for the dairy item

parts.note: curd is a dairy product

explanation.surface: A recipe note: leave out a dairy ingredient from the peanut dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this period of time' points to the day the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle ran on the sixth day of the week, so this day of publication is the weekend day named.

clue.text: Upset cleaner chasing bill for place of worship

indicators.note: chasing means the rearranged letters come after the bill word

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An annoyed cleaner pursues payment from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' makes ERNACLE, and 'chasing' sets it after the bill word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a sanctuary or meeting house used for religious services.

clue.text: Firm blocking most of binoculars with warning regarding type of lens

indicators.note: blocking means the company abbreviation sits in the middle, obstructing
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bins is British slang for binoculars
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
cave is Latin for beware, a schoolboy warning

explanation.surface: A company obstructs most binocular sales, giving a caution about lenses.
explanation.walkthrough: BINS is British slang for binoculars; 'most of' cuts it to BIN, and CAVE (pronounced kay-vee) was a public-school cry of beware.
explanation.definitionFit: A biconcave lens curves inwards on both faces, one kind of optical glass.

clue.text: British are excited with flakes etc, one tucking in — this?

definitions.text: British are excited with flakes etc, one tucking in — this?

indicators.note: tucking in means the single letter is put inside the mixture
excited means stirred up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: one can be the article a

explanation.surface: Britons get thrilled by cornflakes and the like as everyone tucks in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a morning bowl of flakes eaten by a British diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and similar grain flakes are the classic morning dish people tuck into.

clue.text: Article from Spain is reversible fibre

indicators.note: reversible means the phrase can be turned round and read backwards

parts.note: las is a Spanish plural definite article

explanation.surface: A Spanish item of clothing is a reversible fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversible' looks like a description of the fabric but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from agave leaves used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Those people, in short, encountered a tourist in Cornwall

parts.note: 'em is a shortened form of them, those people
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Some locals bumped into a holidaymaker in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in south-west England; locals there call visitors by this old word for an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornish dialect the word, originally meaning ant, is a slightly scornful name for a visiting holidaymaker.

clue.text: Dark clothing not universal early in the day

indicators.note: not means the letter for universal is taken away

parts.note: mourning is the black dress worn after a death
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Black clothes are not for everyone at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not universal' removes U from MOURNING.
explanation.definitionFit: The first part of the day, before noon, is the hours after dawn.

clue.text: They focus here, finally, certainly taking in church after confusion

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of here is used
taking in means the affirmative word swallows the next pieces

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: after means the church letters follow the mess word

parts.note: pie is printer's jargon for a jumbled mess of type
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sermon note: attention here, at last, surely includes church after a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is printer's jargon for jumbled type; 'They focus here' tempts as the definition, but 'here' supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyepieces are the lenses on microscopes and telescopes that are adjusted to sharpen the view.

clue.text: Satisfied with material in book, say

definitions.meaning: happy and at ease with things
what a book holds, such as its text and chapters

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pleased with one's lot, and the noun means the substance contained in a publication.

clue.text: Increased in range of knowledge applied to energy and fuel

indicators.note: applied to means set alongside, so the next letter is added on
in means the went-up word sits inside the knowledge word

parts.note: ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken
rose means went up, increased
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Greater understanding combined with vigour powers one's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN is a range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines is a liquid fuel.

clue.text: Release Cockney dish? That gets a negative response

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, a hunk
not is a negative reply, as in certainly not

explanation.surface: Freeing a London heart-throb, who says no.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, London's East End accent, drops initial H, turning HUNK into UNK.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a tie or tangle is to free or loosen it, a synonym of release.

clue.text: Irritated about exam?

definitions.meaning: a playful sense: having to do with a test, like a test

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means short-tempered, and the question mark admits a whimsical second reading as test-related.

clue.text: Perhaps Brownie cameras aren't key equipment initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: Kodak's Brownie camera may not be essential photo kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brownie looks like Kodak's old camera but is a chocolate bake.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a dense chocolate bake, one example of a sweet baked treat.

clue.text: Alliance backing boundary area

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read from the back

parts.note: in cricket a boundary hit over the rope scores six

explanation.surface: A coalition supports a frontier zone.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a hit to the edge of the field, a six when it clears the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Second World War pact of Germany, Italy and Japan was known by this name, an alliance.

clue.text: Some motorcyclists are leaving to frighten walkers

indicators.note: leaving means those letters depart from the frighten word

parts.note: to scare is to frighten
ramblers are countryside walkers

explanation.surface: Bikers roar off, scaring hikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are leaving' takes ARE out of SCARE, leaving SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders in motocross racing over rough off-road courses are known by this name.

clue.text: Outer garment, note, discarded in Pacific islands

indicators.note: discarded means the note letter is thrown out

parts.note: Tonga is a group of islands in the South Pacific

explanation.surface: A coat and a note are thrown away on a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman toga was a loose robe draped over other clothes.

clue.text: Forcefully appearing in my eleventh game

indicators.note: game here means willing or lively, so these letters are played around with

explanation.surface: Playing hard in my eleventh match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as a match but is the anagram signal for MY ELEVENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with great passion and intensity means acting powerfully, with force.
